verdict.rationale:
Codegen exposes agent-permissions and agent-behavior settings (e.g., requiring explicit mentions to trigger, presenting a structured plan before executing, requiring signed commits) which give some control over agent autonomy, but there is no documented concept of tiered autonomy levels or a granular confirmation-gating system for actions.
missing for 10: explicit tiered autonomy levels (e.g., auto-approve vs. require-approval per action type), a policy engine or role-based confirmation workflow, and independent verification that these settings actually block agent actions pending human approval.
